The primary material of a candle is typically wax, which serves as the fuel source, often accompanied by a wick that draws the liquid wax up to the flame through capillary action.

Regarding the provided text, the book *The Great Society* posits that 1960s welfare programs failed to eradicate poverty and instead fostered dependency. While the author utilizes statistical data to support this view, the text critically notes that this perspective is one-sided. It overlooks the complex socio-economic factors contributing to poverty and ignores systemic issues. Furthermore, it dismisses the positive impacts these programs have had on millions, suggesting that a balanced evaluation must account for both the alleged negative cultural effects and the tangible benefits provided to vulnerable populations.
